en: The Secret Essential Sūtra of the Seven Stars and the Wish-Fulfilling Wheel, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Amoghavajra.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Buddha was at the Gaṅgā River in Nālandā on the Great Snowy Mountains, together with...
There was a great assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus together with him.
Their names were Mahāmaudgalyāyana, Śāriputra, Mahākātyāyana, and Pūrṇa.
Ānanda, Mahākāśyapa, Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra, and furthermore eighteen thousand bodhisattvas.
They all attained the dharani of non-retrogression and eloquence.
Within such assemblies, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River, they turned the great wheel of Dharma.
At that time, there was a palace attendant in the city of Kāśī.
They approached the Buddha, prostrated at his feet, and said to him:
"King Prasenajit has sent us to consult you."
The great kingdom of Kuśinagara has arrived with countless billions of troops to besiege Kāśī.
The ruler and his ministers are in a state of frantic alarm, and the people are filled with fear.
We pray only that the World-Honored One, by means of your great power of wisdom, will protect and deliver us.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva King of Spiritual Powers, saying:
"Go to the palace within the city of Kāśī."
Swiftly establish the secret gateway of the seven-star fire altar for the *Cintāmaṇicakra-bhadrakalpa* maṇḍala.
Regarding what is called the *Bhadrakalpa* maṇḍala:
construct it within a pure chamber.
Construct a fire altar for the Seven Stars in an open space.
Perform the rite according to the ritual rules for one day and one night;
the host of thieves will naturally retreat and disperse.
As for the ritual procedure:
first, one must establish the boundary (sīmābandha), and then perform the Pañjara-dharmaparyāya.
Homage to the Great Dharma Lord, King of the Wish-Fulfilling Wheel (Cintāmaṇicakra).
I now respectfully commission the creation of this paṭola;
may those who possess the divine ear and eye,
and those who possess supernormal powers, bear witness to these dharmic rules.
Then, recite the Cintāmaṇicakra Dhāraṇī seven times; consecrate the water with the mantra seven times and sprinkle it upon the ground.
After establishing the boundary markers, perform the ritual of binding the boundary (sīmābandha).
As for what is called the *paṭṭala*:
first, prepare a most pure chamber with a floor as level as a mirror;
in its center, construct a five-colored wheel-image resembling a chariot wheel.
Whether there be ten spokes or twelve spokes,
one should draw the mark of a vajra on the intervals between them;
it is the same for the spokes of the wheel as well.
In the center, install the Bodhisattva King Amoghapāśa.
Between each of the spokes, install images of the Seven Stars and the Mother Hārītī.
Before each image, arrange various offerings such as lamps, ghee, and incense.
The name of the person for whom the rite is performed is inscribed upon their respective star;
the Ācārya sits outside the wheel.
Thus, each and every ritual procedure shall be accomplished.
Perform the empowered recitation for one session of one hundred and eight repetitions.
If the visualization is not accomplished, do not count the repetitions.
As for what is called the fire altar (homa-maṇḍala):
Construct a fire pit in an open space,
measuring either one cubit or two cubits; then,
consecrate either a single person or a layman (upāsaka) and a laywoman (upāsikā).
Don new, clean garments and prepare offerings for the primary star, such as cakes, ghee, honey, incense, and medicinal herbs. Then, facing the seven stars,
bow once and burn an offering once with single-minded devotion, fixing your mind upon the primary star.
If the light shifts or changes color, one immediately attains accomplishment.
If the ācārya is pure, whether he be a king, a minister, or even a common person, [the same result follows].
If one constructs a fire altar oneself and makes a request,
one will achieve accomplishment immediately according to one's wishes.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Ṛddhirāja...
Immediately following these instructions, he went to the palace within the great city of Kāśī and performed each ritual; thereupon,
thunderbolts and lightning struck, and the bandits were dispersed and destroyed.
The sovereign and his ministers were filled with joy, and the people lived in peace and happiness.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Ṛddhiprabha returned to the presence of the Buddha and prostrated at the Buddha’s feet.
He then addressed the Buddha, saying, "How marvelous, World-Honored One!
This inconceivable dharma-gate of secret mysteries—
where is the Bodhisattva Cintāmaṇicakravartin now?"
"By the power of the Tathāgata,
we have gone to that world to pay homage to the Bodhisattva Cintāmaṇicakra-rāja.
The Buddha then addressed the Bodhisattva Abhijñārāja:
Excellent, excellent!
To the true south there is a world named Seven-Jeweled Wheel-Turning King.
Upon the seven-jeweled wheel, the seven stars that protect the Dharma and various celestial hosts surround it on all sides.
To turn the wheel of Dharma and deliver sentient beings.
At that time, the Bodhisattva King of Supernatural Powers addressed the Buddha, saying:
World-Honored One, for what reason do you not only instruct one to contemplate the Bodhisattva King of the Wish-Fulfilling Wheel,
but also command the worship of one's natal star and so forth?
The Buddha said: "In the past, when the Dīpaṃkara Buddha received this dharma-gate,
the spirits of the seven stars descended from heaven,
and the great deity Hārītī emerged from the earth."
May we, as a group, protect this Great Dharma.
Should there be those who respectfully create this Dharma,
may we arrive first to bring their ritual practices to fulfillment.
For these reasons, the methods for its construction were also preserved.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Ṛddhiprabha, sustained by the great supernormal power of the Buddha, [proceeded].
He went to that world,
prostrated before the Bodhisattva Cintāmaṇicakra-rāja,
and spoke these words:
We dwell within this Sahā world, training in the stages of the Tathāgata’s causal ground to deliver King Prasenajit of Kāśī;
for these reasons, we pay homage to you, O Benevolent One,
a Wheel-Turning King adorned with the seven treasures, whose marks and signs as a Bodhisattva are inconceivable.
With both primary and secondary retributions equally sublime and wondrous, I now pay homage to you, O Cintāmaṇicakra.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Cintāmaṇicakra spoke these verses:
"The path of the bodhisattva which I now cultivate is for the purpose of delivering sentient beings from the sufferings of the long night."
The assembly is now adorned by the Cintāmaṇicakra; may all sentient beings likewise be so.
Whatever aspirations sentient beings in this world possess, may I, the King of the Wish-Fulfilling Jewel-Wheel, provide every kind of enjoyment they receive, fulfilling their hearts as they wish.
If there are sentient beings in the world who, desiring to attain penetration into the path of the unconditioned,
possess deep and heavy karmic obstacles and fail to achieve success, I shall cause them to awaken through the precious wheel.
If calamities of the three disasters arise in any world, and the nations and their people find no peace or joy, [I shall likewise bring them relief].
If there are those within this realm who practice my Dharma, The noble wheel that fulfills wishes shall grant them great bliss.
Should there be thieves from other worlds or realms, Or disturbances from the four directions causing unrest,
If there are people within the kingdom who practice my Dharma, The noble wheel that fulfills wishes shall grant them peace and happiness.
If there be famine and hardship within the realm, and all the people are not at peace or joyful;
if anyone performs my *bhāvanā* dharma, the noble wheel that acts according to their wishes will be able to provide salvation.
If there are sentient beings in the world who are oppressed by royal law or imprisoned in jail, [they too shall be saved].
I have fashioned this great Dharma-vidyā-mantra, the noble wish-fulfilling wheel that can provide salvation.
If there are sentient beings in perilous difficulties, this noble wish-fulfilling wheel can provide salvation.
If there are sentient beings in the world afflicted by various ailments such as blindness, deafness, lameness, or crippledness, [this wheel can provide salvation].
Recall my Great Dharma Pañjara, the noble wish-fulfilling wheel that can provide salvation.
If there are sentient beings in this world who desire a wealthy household or seek riches and official rank,
they should fashion my Great Dharma Pañjara, the noble wish-fulfilling wheel, according to their wishes.
If there is such a Wish-Fulfilling Wheel (Cintāmaṇicakra), No sinful obstructions will remain unremoved,
And no auspiciousness will remain unattained. Reaching everywhere to deliver from suffering—
To all devas, nāgas, spirits, and humans, It is the refuge for all sentient beings.
Not following after the mind, one does not fall into false speech; this Dharma can eliminate all sins and increase all merits.
It possesses the sovereign power to illuminate the five realms of existence and fulfill the vows of all sentient beings. At that time, the Bodhisattva Ṛddhirāja...
I prostrate to the Noble Wheel, which returns to its original place.
With single-minded devotion, one should uphold this inconceivable mahā-vidyā mantra of the secret dharma-gate.

Namo arhataye āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahākāruṇikāya | tadyathā | oṃ cakrāpate cintāmaṇe mahāprati-mare ruru-ti-cakre aṣa hūṃ rephe svāhā || Oṃ praticintāmaṇi mahācakra aḥ hūṃ || Oṃ padmapraticintāmaṇi hūṃ || The mudrā of the Seven Stars’ own family; the fundamental mudrā of Cintāmaṇicakra; the mudrā for long recitation. If a person has something they seek, [they should perform this].
Whether it be for overcoming the hardships of illness, prolonging one's life,
seeking official rank, or any other aspiration of the mind,
one’s natal star shall surely accord with one's wishes.
The Tathāgata, while in the world, established a great vow:
"For this ritual cycle, one should perform homa;
for this purpose, the seven stars shall be employed for their spiritual efficacy."
This is a great secret that must not be transmitted outside. This Dharma was created for kings or for ministers; it must not be created for commoners or for sentient beings of shallow understanding.

Wu (5): *bi*—translated as "small bean food"; *su gu xiang mu*—translated as "sugarcane wood. Wei (6): *duo yi ni*—translated as "large bean food"; *bo zhi tao mu*—translated as "peach wood. Shen (7): *sa po*—translated as "sesame seed food"; *bo*—this is "thornwood. You (8): *su wu di*—translated as "wheat food"; *mi su di wei mu*—translated as "millet wood. Xu (9): *sa po zhi*—translated as "rice food"; *sun su wu rui*—[unidentified]. Hai (10): *po yi su*—translated as "millet food"; *zhou ni*—translated as "locust tree seeds. Sa po ye—translated as "foxtail millet food"; *jie di*—translated as " paulownia wood."
The *Seven-Star Amoghapāśa Secret Essential Sūtra* was completed on the tenth day of the second month of the spring in the fifth year of Tenmei (1785),
at Daibōon-ji Temple in the north of Raku,
using a copy from the collection of Jōrin-in Temple.
This *Saptatāraka-Amoghapāśa-sūtra* was re-collated and verified based on the draft manuscript of the *Jūnyo Jinmitsu Shō*. Written by Jinin,
a student at Chikujin, while residing in Tōbu, in the middle month of autumn in the first year of the Kyōwa era.
Having obtained the original manuscript of the aforementioned work, I ordered it to be transcribed.
It was then collated by Chūrin, Jizaiin, Denpō, and others;
I further examined and verified it before carving it into woodblocks.
Completed with one final revision and additions.
On the seventh day of the fourth month in the third year of Jishun (1059), on this very day, the rain was thick and dim.
Collated and finalized by Shuangjiaoliao; Dragon Liver.
